newsitem.title: UK: World drug sales up 6 pct in 4 months to April-IMS.
newsitem.headline: World drug sales up 6 pct in 4 months to April-IMS.

text.p: Pharmaceutical sales in the world's top ten markets rose by six percent in the first four months of 1997, market researcher IMS International said on Monday.
IMS said North America continued to be the fastest-growing market, with sales in the U.S. rising by 11 percent year-on-year and in Canada by ten percent.

In Europe the rate of growth improved to four percent in local currency terms from three percent, with Spain seeing the fastest rise at nine percent. Germany halted recent falls with a flat performance in local currency terms, enabling it to seize back its position as Europe's largest market for prescription drugs from France.
Growth in Japan slipped to one percent after a gain of six percent in the first three months of the year.

Among therapeutic categories, strongest growth was seen in central nervous system drugs, which rose by 12 percent in the first four months of the year.
IMS said the expansion in anti-depressant drugs, notably Eli Lilly & Co's Prozac and SmithKline Beecham Plc's Seroxat/Paxil have been major drivers for this category, especially in the U.S.
Anti-infectives, which include anti-virals and antibiotics, and sensory organ drug sales each rose by ten percent in local currency terms.
